reviewer: keep the literal `frame.height < slow` rule and leave the boundary ambiguity open as a non-blocking note for the owner
advocate: refuse `frame.height <= slow`, because at height == slow the strategy can never take a position, and pin both sides of the boundary in tests
decision: Refuse when `frame.height <= slow` (exit 2, message "the range has N candles, not more than slow S: the strategy could never take a position; widen the dates or lower --slow"), and add proof tests pinning `--slow 24` on 24 candles to exit 2 and `--slow 23` on 24 candles to exit 0.
rationale: Both verdicts agree on the fact: at height == slow the only possible long signal sits on the last row, which engine.py never fills, so the run always prints 0 trades.

intent.md line 52 gives the rule and its purpose in one clause ("so the strategy could never take a position"); only `<=` satisfies that purpose, and it still refuses every range the literal `<` refuses.
The safer reading is to refuse a run the owner's own words call unusable rather than exit 0 with an empty result that looks like a success (ux-and-brand: designed empty/error states).
The current proof (`--slow 30` on 24 candles) passes under either rule, so the two boundary tests are needed to make the choice deliberate rather than inherited.

Deferred review (decision 21) lets the owner switch back to the literal `<` at the gate if the number, not the reason, was meant; that would be a one-comparison change plus flipping the boundary test.
